title: Uniform simulation of coded machines
statement: For every machine format $F$, there are a finite Turing machine $S$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $d$ such that, for every pair of Boolean words $\alpha,x$ and every $t\in\mathbb N$, on input encoding the pair consisting of the binary representation of $t$ and $\alpha$, paired with $x$, the machine $S$ halts within $d(|\alpha|+|x|+t+1)^d$ steps and outputs the single bit $1$ exactly when the machine denoted by the code decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output $[1]$; otherwise it outputs the single bit $0$.
hypotheses_covered: true case: decoded machine computes $[1]$ from $x$ within $t$ steps
false case: decoded machine does not compute $[1]$ from $x$ within $t$ steps
simulator input is the nested pair encoding of the binary representation of $t$, $\alpha$, and $x$
